text: Lesson 1 named the honest state of Overlook's DR readiness before this project: nobody actually knew if the company would survive a real incident. Overlook did have backups, but a backup existing somewhere is not the same thing as a tested, targeted recovery plan.

A real plan answers two questions in numbers. Recovery Point Objective, or RPO, is the maximum acceptable data loss, measured in time — how far back could the restored data be, worst case. Recovery Time Objective, or RTO, is the maximum acceptable downtime — how long from a disaster being declared to the system being reachable again.

This capstone sets an RPO of 5 minutes and an RTO of 1 hour for Overlook. Appointment bookings and billing entries are business-critical — losing more than a few minutes risks double-bookings and billing errors that directly affect patients. And a healthcare provider's scheduling and billing systems being down for a full business day is a real cost the board explicitly wants to avoid.
These targets only mean something if there's a real mechanism that can hit them. Next lesson builds exactly that: a failover group.
